name: PetaSats
description: Buys BSV with USDC on Base from an AI app through a local MCP server. The kit's keys stay on this device and each swap settles as a cross-chain atomic swap with the counterparty. Quote and status tools keep your existing policy; the swap, the two withdrawal tools, close_kit, buy_gas and pay_402 move funds and need review. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: Keep swap_asset_to_bsv, withdraw_bsv, withdraw_base, close_kit, buy_gas and pay_402 on review: each one moves funds. get_quote, fund_wallet and list_liquidity are read-only and move nothing.

Create ~/.petasats/limits.json: bsvDestinations and baseDestinations allowlist where swaps and withdrawals send funds, maxSwapUsdPerDay caps daily swaps, and x402MaxSatsPerCall and x402MaxSatsPerDay cap pay_402, which pays each service's own address.
Keep shell and file-write access to ~/.petasats on review: an agent that can edit limits.json or the STOP file can undo those limits. The kit rereads limits.json before every money operation.
Use stop_spending to stop new swaps, withdrawals and payments at once. Only the user can resume, from a terminal (npx petasats-mcp@0.2.24 resume); recovery of swaps already started keeps working.
Leave speed at standard, the default, which waits for one BSV confirmation, or set allowFastSettlement to false. Fast settlement accepts an unconfirmed BSV lock and is limited to $25.
Never let an agent read, print or send ~/.petasats/keys.json; it holds the only copy of the kit's keys, so keep a private backup.
Pin the package version when launching with npx (for example petasats-mcp@0.2.24) so only the reviewed release runs.

Connect with the npx entry from the README (npx -y petasats-mcp@0.2.24). The absolute node path that `petasats-mcp init` prints is not this listing's launcher, so Guard does not apply this policy to it.
